proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide that is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte. Its phosphate network resists oxidation near 4 V and it is a well-known protective coating for cathodes in sulfide cells, so it should minimize interfacial penalty while keeping the band gap above 2 eV.

Its Li-Nb-O network should have fewer thermodynamically favourable contact reactions with Li6PS5Cl than the Li3PO4 that gave a penalty of 0.34 eV/atom, so it may come closer to the 0.05 eV/atom acceptance threshold.

proposal.hypothesis: LiCl is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-ion halide whose anion matches the Cl in Li6PS5Cl and whose cation (Li+) cannot be reduced by the sulfide.
